_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an index averaging key soft commodities coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice with a base of 100 in 2015, now stands at 132, reflecting a 32% rise since then. This headline increase points to a notable but uneven climb, as prices have not moved uniformly across the components over the period. The upward trend is relatively recent and corresponds to fluctuations in specific commodity markets rather than a broad-based inflation across all basket items. As such, the composite index conveys a weighted average impact, not synchronized price changes across every included good.
notes.movers: Coffee prices have surged by 93% since 2015, the largest increase in the basket, while orange juice has risen 22%. Wheat and sugar showed more modest rises, 7% and 5% respectively. These disparities owe largely to weather disruptions and crop diseases, such as frost, drought in arabica coffee regions, and citrus greening affecting orange juice, underscoring the vulnerability of these thin, specialized soft-commodity markets where supply shocks can sharply affect global prices. The price dynamics reflect localized agricultural risks rather than generalized inflationary pressures.
notes.why: The headline rise in the breakfast basket is driven by a few weather- and disease-exposed crops, highlighting the sensitivity of thinly traded soft commodities to environmental factors. Such shocks can lead to sustained period of elevated prices due to production uncertainties. Consequently, inputs to this index may remain volatile and elevated over multiple years depending on climatic and agricultural conditions.
